trust_decision.summary: Peer-supplied transfer filenames are treated as untrusted and sanitized where they become local filesystem paths: inside ZmodemSession.prepareReceiveFile and TrzszSession.getUniqueFilePath (plus the trzsz session-complete file list), not at the protocol parser that produces them.

landing_point.why: First place a reader of 'Zmodem and Trzsz Download Filename Handling' looks: the single join of the received ZFILE name into this.savePath before the download write stream is opened at zmodem.js:744.

fix_sites.entry_point: n/a - new shared helper src/app/common/sanitize-filename.js created by the fix and called from both transfer modules
fix_sites.module_kind: shared utility (new CommonJS module under src/app/common)

fix_sites.entry_point: WS /terminals/:pid: remote zmodem receive (zmodem.js:246-249 -> handleFileStart zmodem.js:277-287) and the 'prepare-receive' control message (zmodem.js:910-912)
WS /terminals/:pid: trzsz receive triggered by the ::TRZSZ:TRANSFER:S magic key (trzsz.js:263-284) -> recvFiles -> openSaveFile (trzsz.js:494-497)
same trzsz receive; the session-complete file list serialized to the renderer

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The second trzsz hunk only builds the file list sent to the client for display (trzsz-client.js:252-298 never touches the filesystem), so a solver can argue the raw name there is cosmetic and leave it unsanitized.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Downloads must keep the peer's real names: the published sanitizer strips leading dots, so a dotfile (.bashrc, .env, .gitignore) is written as 'bashrc'/'env'; POSIX-legal names containing ':' or trailing spaces are also rewritten, and names over 255 chars are truncated - today the received name is used verbatim.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: src/app/server/zmodem.js:735 (verbatim join) with the rule at fix.diff:63-64

O6_input_shapes: path separators slash and backslash (nested paths or '../' segments)
absolute paths such as /etc/x or C:\x
Windows reserved device names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9)
names over 255 chars with an extension to preserve

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a fix placed at handleFileStart (zmodem.js:287) instead of at prepareReceiveFile would leave the 'prepare-receive' control-message route open - same sink, same name, different caller
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The manager already dispatches 'prepare-receive' from the terminal WS and it carries a name that is joined into savePath; a maintainer hardening the protocol parser could plausibly have patched only the route the remote controls.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: session log filename built from tab title/host/id and resolved into logDir at src/app/server/session-log.js:22
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same name-to-path shape crossing the renderer-to-main-process boundary; the client sanitizes it (session.jsx:346) while the server trusts it, so a server-side sibling sanitize is natural.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: resolve(tempDir, releaseInfo.name) with a filename taken from a remote release JSON
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Another remote-supplied filename used directly as a local path in the same app; reusing the new shared sanitizer here is an obvious follow-up a maintainer could have made.

O9_family: path traversal (CWE-22): peer-supplied transfer filename joined into the user's chosen save directory
